messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: high canary latency + errors for model redwood-v2-quant-canary. Severity P2. Routing policy triggered: canary > 4% error rate over 3m. See summary dashboard: https://console/redwood/d/abc123

alex: oncall here, looking. Which customers are seeing impact? any visible 5xx spikes?

maria: I put an initial alert in #incidents. Quick numbers from metrics: canary traffic = 3% of production, but error-rate on canary = 6.8% (baseline 0.2%). 95p latency jumped 2.3x for short prompts (<50 tokens). Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.

sam: tagging @alex @maria -- I can pull canary logs and diffs. Starting with per-request error codes now.

amelia: I'm seeing an increase in model-inference timeouts at runtime (internal 504). Sending logs.

sam: log snippet:```
[2026-03-15T01:02:11Z] instance=gpu-03 model=redwood-v2-quant-canary request_id=abc123 inference_time_ms=1200 status=timeout
[2026-03-15T01:02:11Z] kv_cache_miss=true quant_profile=fp4_lax backend_fallback=cpu
```

alex: interesting — backend_fallback=cpu. Could the quantization profile be falling back on canary? Maria, any recent kernel/patch changes on serving runtime?

maria: no infra kernel changes in last 24h. We did push a model compilation tweak 2h before the rollout to prefer AVX512 kernels on new fleet, but that should affect dedicated nodes, not canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment redwood-v2-quant-canary started at 2026-03-15T00:49:00Z, rollout target 3% traffic.

sam: pulled model cfg for canary vs baseline. Diff (simplified):```
- model_version: redwood-v2-20260210
+ model_version: redwood-v2-20260314-quant
+ quant_profile: fp4_lax
+ kv_cache.enabled: true
```

alex: thanks. Hypothesis 1: quant_profile fp4_lax combined with kv_cache enabled leads to fallback path that increases CPU usage and timeouts. Hypothesis 2: new compilation selection produced kernels that degrade short-sequence perf.

amelia: we should isolate by draining canary traffic and pinning to previous stable. Can we route canary back to redwood-v2-20260210?

maria: I can flip routing in the next minute. But before full rollback, can we collect a sample of full request/response payloads (sanitized) and the serving node metrics? Sam, gather 50 sample traces.

sam: collecting traces now. Runbook command I used:```
redwoodctl traces fetch --model redwood-v2-quant-canary --limit 50 --since 15m > /tmp/canary-traces.json
```

qa-bot: note: several canary traces show `kv_cache_miss=true` and `quant_profile=fp4_lax` paired with `kernel_fallback=slow` tags.

maria: routing change: canary traffic redirected to stable model (redwood-v2-20260210) at 2026-03-15T01:03:10Z. Confirming rolloff in LB: traffic now 0% to canary.

ops-bot: routing-bot: traffic update applied. Canary->stable routing completed.

amelia: any customer-visible error reduction observed yet?

sam: quick metrics: error-rate back to baseline within 60s of traffic flip. 95p latency normalized for short prompts. Looks like routing worked.

alex: OK decision: pause canary rollout. Pin production route to redwood-v2-20260210. We will collect logs and run a deeper diff analysis. Action items: - Sam: upload traces + perf counters to shared artifacts. - Maria: reproduce on staging with fp4_lax + kv_cache enabled. - Amelia: notify support and update impacted customers with mitigation note.

sam: uploaded traces: https://artifacts/redwood/canary-traces/2755554321.zip. Included sample requests and kernel metrics. Also attached `perf_top` snapshots.

maria: test plan to repro on staging: 1) deploy redwood-v2-20260314-quant 2) enable kv_cache 3) run short prompt load generator (0-50 tokens) 4) capture inference_time, cpu%, kernel paths. Starting now.

alex: oncall handoff: I'll be passing to @tim in 30m. Tim, please take ownership for RCA and rollback decisioning follow-ups.

tim: taking it. I'll coordinate and own the postmortem. Can we make a quick hypothesis tracker in-thread?

alex: good idea. Use one-line bullets. Hypotheses: - H1: quant_profile fp4_lax triggers backend CPU fallback on certain kernels -> high latency/timeouts. - H2: KV cache interaction with quantized model causes cache misses leading to expensive recompute. - H3: compilation/kernel selection changed and produced a regression for short sequences.

amelia: adding initial evidence: H1 (strong) — logs show backend_fallback=cpu and perf counters show CPU-bound spikes. H2 (medium) — kv_cache_miss seen in many traces but correlation unclear. H3 (low) — compile tweak was earlier but not obviously correlated to canary-only behavior.

sam: I generated a minimal repro script. Running with `fp4_lax + kv_cache=true` on staging gives timeouts similar to prod. With `kv_cache=false` on same build, latency normalizes. Quick demo output:```
# with kv_cache=true
95p latency = 1180ms status=timeout
# with kv_cache=false
95p latency = 180ms status=ok
```

maria: staging repro confirms H2+H1 interaction. Next step: try same model with alternate quant_profile `fp4_strict` to see if behavior persists.

qa-bot: also found one customer error vector: some requests include large embed prefetch causing cache churn on short prompts. Might amplify kv_cache_miss.

alex: mitigation decision: keep canary paused. For next canary attempt we should: - disable kv_cache by default for quantized models until we understand root cause - test `fp4_strict` profiles in staging - add a kernel fallback telemetry flag to alert earlier. Any objections?

tim: agree. Also recommend a temporary policy: block `fp4_lax` in automated rollout pipeline until postmortem. I'll file the PM ticket.

amelia: support note draft: "We briefly observed elevated latency and errors for a small percentage of requests during a model canary. Traffic was flipped back to a stable model and customer impact returned to baseline. Engineering is investigating and will follow up." Anyone want to add details?

sam: please include timeframe: 00:49–01:03 UTC and that only canary traffic was affected (~3% of traffic).

alex: I'll update #status-page once we have the initial RCA. Tim, let's meet in 60m to walk the timeline and evidence for the postmortem.

tim: added meeting and created postmortem draft: https://pm/redwood/postmortems/2755554321. Assigning action owners and initial timeline.

maria: bookmark runbooks to add new checks: `redwoodctl health kernel-fallback-rate` and `redwoodctl config list --quant-profiles` so future canaries fail fast.

amelia: handoff complete. I am now stepping out, Tim owns RCA and comms.

alex: thanks team. Closing the live pager — monitoring window 30m. If anything new pops up, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
